Summary: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2020 was awarded for discoveries about black holes. Roger Penrose received half the prize "for the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity," while Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez jointly received the other half "for the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy." The award was made on October 6, 2020.

Roger Penrose showed that the general theory of relativity leads to the formation of black holes. Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez discovered that an invisible and extremely heavy object governs the orbits of stars at the centre of our galaxy. A supermassive black hole is the only currently known explanation.
